name: Refugee Status Determination

requirements.blocker_text: The National Committee for Assistance to Refugees (CNAR, created by Décret n° 1978-266 and reorganized by Décret n° 99-310 of 31 December 1999) and the Refugee Status Eligibility Commission (CESR, a 6-member panel including a UNHCR voting member) determine refugee status under a 2001 Eligibility Decree. Rejections may be appealed within 30 days to the Refugee Appeal Commission, whose decision is final. Congo is party to the 1951 Refugee Convention, its 1967 Protocol, and the 1969 OAU Convention -- but per a 2007/2008-vintage secondary source, Congo restricted the 1951 Convention's application to a GEOGRAPHIC reservation covering only European refugees and opted out of the Protocol's dispute-resolution provisions; this dataset could not independently confirm against the UN Treaty Collection whether this reservation remains in force as of 2026. A comprehensive national refugee law, drafted with UNHCR assistance, was reportedly submitted to Parliament in 2006; this dataset found no information confirming whether it has since been adopted.
requirements.fix_path: File a refugee status claim with CNAR/CESR; this dataset could not confirm the exact registration steps or filing deadlines beyond the 30-day appeal window.

outcome.duration_length: 5-year renewable identity card, tied to continued protection needs

sources.title: USCRI World Refugee Survey 2008, Congo-Brazzaville chapter (an NGO secondary report, hosted on Refworld) -- CNAR/CESR structure, 2001 Eligibility Decree, refugee rights, 1951 Convention geographic reservation, status of the 2006 draft refugee law

STATUS: DRAFT -- correctly tier-3 sourced from the outset (this is an NGO advocacy-organization annual survey; being hosted on Refworld does not make it tier 2, since tier here tracks the content's own authorship/type, not the hosting domain -- a government LAW hosted on Refworld is tier 2, but an NGO SURVEY hosted on Refworld is tier 3, consistent with this dataset's convention). GENUINE, UNUSUAL FINDING not seen elsewhere in this dataset: Congo reportedly limited its 1951 Refugee Convention accession to a geographic reservation covering only European refugees -- if still in force, this is a materially different legal posture than every other country built in this session that is party to the Convention. This could NOT be independently verified against the UN Treaty Collection's official reservations list in this build, so it is flagged as an important open question rather than settled fact. Separately, a comprehensive national refugee law drafted with UNHCR assistance was reportedly submitted to Parliament in 2006 (per an 18-year-old source) -- whether it was ever adopted could not be confirmed; Congo's own government legal-text portals could not be fetched at all in this build (see other cg/ files' notes on gov.cg fetch failures). work_rights set to 'full' and study_rights to 'restricted' per the Eligibility Decree's own described terms ('same treatment as nationals' for employment; social aid/education covered only 'to the extent possible').
